description: Machine-readable inventory of architecture audit checks: dependency structure, module design, change risk, and data flow and decisions.

statusTaxonomy.partial: The invariant mostly holds, with exceptions, or a soft check shows mixed adherence.
statusTaxonomy.violation: Concrete code or configuration breaks the invariant.

enrichmentFlags.description: Run installed boundary and dead-code tools (dependency-cruiser, madge, knip) to confirm collector results.

checks.title: No import cycles
checks.rationale: Cycles make load order fragile and stop any part of the cycle from being changed, tested, or extracted on its own.
checks.expectation: Runtime imports form no cycles. Type-only imports are excluded.
checks.violationSignal: One or more cycles among runtime imports, each reported as the importing lines that form it.

checks.title: Boundaries enforced by tooling
checks.rationale: A boundary that nothing enforces erodes one convenient import at a time, and agents take the shortest path that compiles.
checks.expectation: A boundary tool (dependency-cruiser, eslint-plugin-boundaries, Nx module boundaries, or a restricted-paths or no-cycle rule) encodes the dependency rules and runs in a package script or continuous integration.
checks.violationSignal: No boundary tool, or one that is configured but run by nothing.

checks.title: Dependencies point the declared way
checks.rationale: When lower layers import higher ones, a change to the user interface can break the domain, and nothing can be reused or tested in isolation.
checks.expectation: Domain and shared code do not import user-interface, framework, or infrastructure code; sibling features reach each other only through public entry points.
checks.violationSignal: An import against the declared or inferred direction, reported with the importing line and the rule it breaks.

checks.title: Module internals are unreachable
checks.rationale: Internals that can be imported become part of the interface, so they can never change without breaking a caller.
checks.expectation: Code outside a feature or package imports only its public entry point, and something (a package `exports` map, a boundary rule, or a lint error) makes importing internals fail.
checks.violationSignal: Imports that reach into another feature's or package's internal files.

checks.title: Workspaces import each other through entry points
checks.rationale: Relative imports across workspaces bypass the published contract, so a refactor inside one package silently breaks another.
checks.expectation: Workspaces import each other by package name through published entry points. Not applicable outside multi-package workspaces.
checks.violationSignal: A relative import from one workspace into another workspace's files. Test-only cases are graded partial.

checks.title: Modules are deep
checks.rationale: Shallow modules spread one concept across many files, so every change touches several and callers must understand the implementation anyway.
checks.expectation: Important modules hide substantial behaviour behind a small interface; deleting one would concentrate complexity rather than just move it.
checks.violationSignal: A shallow module: an interface nearly as complex as its implementation, or callers coordinating several calls to complete one operation, reported with the deletion-test result.

checks.title: No pass-through layers
checks.rationale: A layer that only forwards calls adds indirection without hiding anything, and every change has to be threaded through it.
checks.expectation: Every layer adds policy, adaptation, or a distinct abstraction.
checks.violationSignal: A wrapper, service, or hook that forwards the same arguments to another with the same shape.

checks.title: Each piece of state has one owner
checks.rationale: When several modules write the same state, their rules diverge and the product shows stale or contradictory data.
checks.expectation: Each store, cache entry, table, or shared object has one writer; other modules read it or ask the owner to change it.
checks.violationSignal: More than one module writes the same state, reported with each writer.

checks.title: One supported way to do each task
checks.rationale: Two ways to do the same thing both keep gaining callers, because people and agents copy whichever they find first.
checks.expectation: Each recurring task (fetching, dates, forms, feature flags, logging) has one supported mechanism.
checks.violationSignal: Two or more mechanisms for the same task in active use, reported with an example of each.

checks.title: No hand-synced lists
checks.rationale: A list repeated by hand in several places goes out of sync the first time someone updates only the copy they can see.
checks.expectation: Each list of items (routes, permissions, feature names, enum values) has one source that the others derive from, or a check that fails when they disagree.
checks.violationSignal: The same items listed in two or more places with no derivation or consistency check.

checks.title: Representations stay behind interfaces
checks.rationale: When wire, storage, or framework types leak across layers, a schema change ripples through code that should not have known about it.
checks.expectation: External data is parsed into domain types at the boundary; transport, storage, and framework types stay inside the module that owns them.
checks.violationSignal: Wire or storage types re-exported or used deep inside other layers, reported with the leaking import or type.

checks.title: Code grouped by what it knows
checks.rationale: Organising by execution stage (load, validate, transform, save) repeats one representation and its rules across several modules.
checks.expectation: Modules are organised around the knowledge and decisions they own, not the order in which code runs.
checks.violationSignal: Stage-named modules that each re-implement knowledge of the same representation.

checks.title: Hotspots are cohesive and tested
checks.rationale: The files that change most often carry the most risk; a large, mixed, untested hotspot is where regressions come from.
checks.expectation: The most frequently changed files are cohesive and covered by tests at their interface.
checks.violationSignal: A top hotspot that is large, mixes responsibilities, or has no tests that exercise it.

checks.title: Files that change together live together
checks.rationale: Files in different areas that always change together reveal a hidden dependency the structure does not show.
checks.expectation: Files that repeatedly change together sit in the same module or feature, or the coupling is explained.
checks.violationSignal: Strong change coupling between files in different features or packages with no structural reason.

checks.title: Hub modules are stable
checks.rationale: A module that many others import and that itself imports a lot magnifies every change in both directions.
checks.expectation: Modules with high fan-in import little and change rarely; barrels that only re-export are judged by what they expose.
checks.violationSignal: A module with both high fan-in and high fan-out, or high fan-in and frequent change, reported with its counts.

checks.title: No orphaned modules
checks.rationale: Unused modules mislead readers and agents, who copy dead patterns as if they were current.
checks.expectation: Every source module is reachable from an entry point, a route, a test, or configuration.
checks.violationSignal: Modules nothing imports and that are not entry points, verified before reporting.

checks.title: Server state has one home
checks.rationale: Fetching the same data in several ad hoc ways causes waterfalls, duplicated caches, and inconsistent loading and error states.
checks.expectation: Server data is loaded in one designated place: a query layer (TanStack Query, SWR, RTK Query, Apollo), or the framework's server-side data primitives (Server Components, loaders, Server Actions).
checks.violationSignal: Client components fetching directly with useEffect and fetch, or more than one data-fetching strategy, where the framework or a query layer should own it.

checks.title: One client-state strategy
checks.rationale: Several global state libraries split the application's state across incompatible models.
checks.expectation: Global client state uses one strategy; React context is used for dependency injection and stable values, not as a second store.
checks.violationSignal: Two or more global state libraries in use with no stated migration.

checks.title: Side effects sit at the edges
checks.rationale: Storage, cookies, and window access scattered through components make behaviour hard to test and to change.
checks.expectation: Components reach browser storage, cookies, and globals through a hook or service module.
checks.violationSignal: Direct storage, cookie, or window access in component files.

checks.title: Decisions are recorded and still hold
checks.rationale: Without recorded decisions, every review re-litigates them; decisions the code no longer follows mislead everyone who reads them.
checks.expectation: Hard-to-reverse architectural decisions are recorded, for example as architecture decision records, and the code still follows them.
checks.violationSignal: No record of the major decisions, or code that contradicts a recorded decision.

checks.title: Domain language is consistent
checks.rationale: When one concept has several names, people and agents build duplicates of it.
checks.expectation: Each domain concept has one name in code and documentation, ideally defined in a glossary.
checks.violationSignal: The same concept named differently across modules. Soft check — mixed adherence is reported as partial.
